jobs.description:

Our SkyOS solution, rigorously and relentlessly developed by skilled and dedicated Skyrysers, is the key to unlocking this unbounded future. Our technology, combined with our commitment to saving lives and our passion for aviation, will empower everyone to experience the joy and freedom of flight.
JUNIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER - EL SEGUNDO, CA

This role is based in our El Segundo office. As a Junior Software Engineer, you will take part in designing, developing and integrating our SkyOS software. You will be given projects and tasks to help develop, enhance throughput and develop tools for the flight software.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Design software logic in embedded C/C++, python, or Rust
Utilize scopes and logic analyzers for debugging and troubleshooting during hardware software integration
Support the development of tools that are necessary to retrieve and monitor critical data
Work with cross-functional teams to support requirement generation and SIL (System In Loop) testing
Analyze the throughput of software and brainstorm ways to improve it

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering or equivalent
Self-motivated, curious, and comfortable working through ambiguous problems with guidance from senior engineers.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or equivalent
Experience in Matlab/Simulink
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and build systems.
Experience deploying, administering, and supporting engineering tools across an organization.
Experience with containerization and infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Docker, Terraform, Ansible).

WHY SKYRYSE?

The opportunity to change the world through improving aviation safety and accessibility 
Salary Range: 125k - 135k
Valuable stock option plan
Heavily subsidized medical, dental and vision plans
Full-time employees are eligible for 20 days of paid time off (PTO) and 5 sick days annually.  PTO and sick days must be used in accordance with Company policy.
A company with an ambitious vision, a dynamic work environment, and a team of smart, motivated, and fun to work-with colleagues!

The posted salary range reflects the potential base pay for this role, adjusted to account for varying geographic markets. Final compensation will be based on factors such as your location, job-related skills, experience, and internal alignment, including equity and benefits.
WE WELCOME ALL

Skyryse is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are seeking a graduate-level intern specializing in front-end engineering or full-stack product development to help turn front-end product screens into real working software functionality inside an existing codebase.

This role is centered around using Claude Code,
Codex
and MCP tools
in the terminal to analyze codebases, review designs and backend documentation, create missing front-end documentation, implement features, debug issues, and refine production-ready software. Claude
may also be used for backend-related tasks and code reviews where appropriate.
This role is about building real product functionality.

The intern’s job is to take front-end screens, flows, and product requirements and help translate them into complete working features by thinking through:

how the feature should behave
what user stories need to be defined
what the acceptance criteria should be
what happens in edge cases
what the data limitations are

and Codex

is required.

jobs.title: Junior Machine Learning Engineer - Rokt Residency
jobs.description:
We are Rokt.

We are the global leader in ecommerce, on a mission to make every transaction more relevant. We’ve built our business around the Transaction Moment™, the span from cart to confirmation where customer attention and intent peak, and where more than 90% of a business’s ancillary revenue potential sits untapped.
The Rokt Brain leverages advanced machine learning to determine the next best action for every customer in real time across the Rokt Network, powering 13 billion transactions a year for brands like: Live Nation, Fanatics, Macy’s, AMC Theatres, PayPal, Uber, Hulu, Albertsons and more. Since 2012 we’ve grown from a Sydney startup, to a $3.5B company with 700+ Rokt’stars across eight offices and 15 markets, sustaining a Compound Annual Growth Rate of 40%+ for over a decade.

At Rokt, we practice transparency in career paths and compensation
, which is why we have a well-defined career ladder with clear compensation and career paths based on competency and ability.
Compensation for this role is ~$50.48/hour. In addition, you will receive a generous technology allowance to spend on a Macbook Pro M5 + accessories: yours to keep after the residency.
If you secure a full-time offer post-residency, total target compensation will be $127,000, including a fixed annual salary of $120,000, employee equity plan grant (RSUs), and world-class benefits.
This is the expected pay for the role. Final compensation is determined by the level assessed through the interview process and based on how your experience and skills map to our career ladder.

About The Role

The Rokt Residency is an 18-week, full-time, paid early-career program for software engineers working out of our office in New York City. This cohort of residencies will kick off January 2027, with the option for earlier start dates for candidates available sooner.
Residents will have the opportunity to receive full-time offers to join Rokt as Builders on the completion of their residency.

How Your Future Team Uses AI

We are an AI-first company. We’re a team of builders. That means the person who spots the problem is usually the person who fixes it, and “someone should build a tool for that” is treated as a volunteer sign-up sheet. We use AI and automation tools to move faster, and expect you to figure things out when the path isn’t obvious. If you prefer established processes and clearly defined lanes, you probably won’t like it here.
Rokt Builders use AI coding agents to write, test, and review code, which means a small team ships what used to take a large one. ML teams use AI to prototype modelling approaches, write and debug training and evaluation code, and analyse experiment results. Residents get the same enterprise AI tools from day one and are expected to use them to build faster.

Team Placement:

You’ll be placed where you can have the most impact, based on your interview performance, prior experience, and business need. We can’t guarantee a specific team, but every Rokt engineering team works heavily with AI, building critical services on modern, complex technology. Rokt’stars move into new teams and projects internally often. Your first team likely won’t be your last.

Machine Learning at Rokt

Every time a customer completes a purchase (the Transaction Moment), the Rokt Brain, our machine learning decision engine, decides which offer to show them. Rokt’s proprietary recommendation systems predict how each customer will respond to each offer, and our auction and decisioning logic uses those predictions to choose what each customer sees across a marketplace of ecommerce brands, advertisers, and customers. Residents on this track work alongside Applied Scientists and ML Engineers to build, test, deploy, and improve models that run in production at a scale of billions of transactions a year.

How You Will Contribute

Build, train, and evaluate machine learning models that predict how customers respond to offers.
Deploy models into production and monitor their performance, robustness, and scalability.
Design and analyse experiments that test whether a new model or approach improves results.
Build and use AI tools and automations to speed up coding, testing, and deployment.
Work with Applied Scientists, product managers, and senior Builders to turn business problems into practical ML solutions.

What you bring:

Required
Strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, and how to write clean, tested code
Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Go, Java, C#, Rust, TypeScript, or Python
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools to build software
Software engineering experience, including internships, personal projects, open-source work, or hackathons
Evidence that you have built and shipped something real, such as a project, product, or tool that other people use
Drive: you hold yourself to a high and rising bar and take ownership beyond your assigned task
Reasoning ability: you break hard problems down from first principles and notice the details that matter
Brilliant and humble: you back the best idea, not just your own, and you’re quick to help a teammate
Availability to work full time in the office in New York, for the full 18 weeks

Preferred
Foundational understanding of statistics, probability, and core ML concepts such as model evaluation, overfitting, and feature engineering
Experience building with PyTorch or TensorFlow, or projects in recommendation systems, deep learning, reinforcement learning, or Bayesian methods

About Rokt’stars:

We move fast and decide with incomplete information, because a good decision this week can lead to a perfect one next quarter. We work as one team, which means the best idea wins regardless of who raised it or what level they are. We hire people who are brilliant and humble and who are obsessed with making the customer successful.

Benefits

During the Residency

Every employee has enterprise access to leading AI tools with generous usage limits, building AI fluency as a core skill
Catered lunch every day and a fully stocked pantry
Dog-friendly offices so you can bring your best friend to work
Generous Required Technology Allowance

If You Join Full Time

Fully funded insurance (Medical, Dental, Vision)
Dollar-for-dollar 401K matching plan (up to 4% of fixed annual salary)
Fully funded life, short term, and long term disability insurance
Equity in a profitable, fast-growing company approaching $1 Billion in revenue
Monthly Wellness and Cell Phone Allowances
Quarterly performance reviews for most roles, so feedback and promotion decisions don’t wait
Extra leave (bonus annual leave, sabbatical leave etc.)
Work in the office with your team at least 4 days a week, because we believe we are better together.

What we look for:

We look for clear evidence of excellence. We value academic achievements, but school & GPA aren’t everything! Your achievements competing in hackathons, launching startups, working in industry, volunteering for stretch projects, or building in your own time all add weight. So if you’ve shipped real work but don’t have a perfect résumé, apply anyway.

At Rokt, we choose to create a company that is as diverse and inclusive as the world we live in by attracting, growing and keeping the best talent. Equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

If this sounds like a role you’d enjoy, apply here, and you’ll hear from our recruiting team.

NOTE: Rokt only contacts candidates from @rokt.com addresses. We never request payment, bank details, or identity documents before a written offer, and we never interview solely over chat apps. Verify any role at rokt.com/careers if you’re unsure.

jobs.title: Junior Infrastructure Software Engineer - Rokt Residency
jobs.description:
We are Rokt.

We are the global leader in ecommerce, on a mission to make every transaction more relevant. We’ve built our business around the Transaction Moment™, the span from cart to confirmation where customer attention and intent peak, and where more than 90% of a business’s ancillary revenue potential sits untapped.

The Rokt Brain leverages advanced machine learning to determine the next best action for every customer in real time across the Rokt Network, powering 13 billion transactions a year for brands like: Live Nation, Fanatics, Macy’s, AMC Theatres, PayPal, Uber, Hulu, Albertsons and more. Since 2012 we’ve grown from a Sydney startup, to a $3.5B company with 700+ Rokt’stars across eight offices and 15 markets, sustaining a Compound Annual Growth Rate of 40%+ for over a decade.

At Rokt, we practice transparency in career paths and compensation
, which is why we have a well-defined career ladder with clear compensation and career paths based on competency and ability.
Compensation for this role is ~$50.48/hour. In addition, you will receive a generous technology allowance to spend on a Macbook Pro M5 + accessories: yours to keep after the residency.
If you secure a full-time offer post-residency, total target compensation will be $127,000, including a fixed annual salary of $120,000, employee equity plan grant (RSUs), and world-class benefits.
This is the expected pay for the role. Final compensation is determined by the level assessed through the interview process and based on how your experience and skills map to our career ladder.

About The Role

The Rokt Residency is an 18-week, full-time, paid early-career program for software engineers working out of our office in New York City. This cohort of residencies will kick off January 2027, with the option for earlier start dates for candidates available sooner.
Residents will have the opportunity to receive full-time offers to join Rokt as Builders on the completion of their residency.

How Your Future Team Uses AI

We are an AI-first company. We’re a team of builders. That means the person who spots the problem is usually the person who fixes it, and “someone should build a tool for that” is treated as a volunteer sign-up sheet. We use AI and automation tools to move faster, and expect you to figure things out when the path isn’t obvious. If you prefer established processes and clearly defined lanes, you probably won’t like it here.
Rokt Builders use AI coding agents to write, test, and review code, which means a small team ships what used to take a large one. Infrastructure teams use AI to write and review infrastructure code, detect and triage incidents, and build the automation other engineers rely on. Residents get the same enterprise AI tools from day one and are expected to use them to build faster.

Team Placement:

You’ll be placed where you can have the most impact, based on your interview performance, prior experience, and business need. We can’t guarantee a specific team, but every Rokt engineering team works heavily with AI, building critical services on modern, complex technology. Rokt’stars move into new teams and projects internally often.

Infrastructure at Rokt

Every time a customer completes a purchase (the Transaction Moment), the Rokt Brain, our machine learning decision engine, decides which offer to show them. Every Rokt engineering team builds those systems on a shared platform critical to billions of transactions a year. Our Platform and Infrastructure teams build and operate that platform: Kubernetes on AWS EKS, core compute and networking including the Istio service mesh, storage and messaging systems such as Kafka and Cassandra, CI/CD pipelines built on GitHub and Buildkite, and observability through Datadog. Residents on this track build and operate the infrastructure and developer tooling that enables every Builder at Rokt.

How You Will Contribute

Build and operate distributed network, storage, database, and compute systems.
Design, build, and improve CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling that Rokt’s engineers use to build, test, and deploy code safely.
Write infrastructure as code that replaces manual work and makes systems easier to operate.
Build and use AI tools and automations to speed up coding, testing, and deployment.
Work cross-functionally to enhance platform capabilities, and increase efficiency & performance.

What you bring:

Required
Strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, and how to write clean, tested code
Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Go, Java, C#, Rust, TypeScript, or Python
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools to build software
Software engineering experience, including internships, personal projects, open-source work, or hackathons
Evidence that you have built and shipped something real, such as a project, product, or tool that other people use
Drive: you hold yourself to a high and rising bar and take ownership beyond your assigned task
Reasoning ability: you break hard problems down from first principles and notice the details that matter
Brilliant and humble: you back the best idea, not just your own, and you’re quick to help a teammate
Availability to work full time in the office in New York, for the full 18 weeks

Preferred
Foundational understanding of OS, database, storage, and network technologies
Experience with public cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) technologies.

About Rokt’stars:

We move fast and decide with incomplete information, because a good decision this week can lead to a perfect one next quarter. We work as one team, which means the best idea wins regardless of who raised it or what level they are. We hire people who are brilliant and humble and who are obsessed with making the customer successful.

Benefits

During the Residency

Every employee has enterprise access to leading AI tools with generous usage limits, building AI fluency as a core skill
Catered lunch every day and a fully stocked pantry
Dog-friendly offices so you can bring your best friend to work
Generous Required Technology Allowance

If You Join Full Time

Fully funded insurance (Medical, Dental, Vision)
Dollar-for-dollar 401K matching plan (up to 4% of fixed annual salary)
Fully funded life, short term, and long term disability insurance
Equity in a profitable, fast-growing company approaching $1 Billion in revenue
Monthly Wellness and Cell Phone Allowances
Quarterly performance reviews for most roles, so feedback and promotion decisions don’t wait
Extra leave (bonus annual leave, sabbatical leave etc.)
Work in the office with your team at least 4 days a week, because we believe we are better together.

What we look for:

We look for clear evidence of excellence. We value academic achievements, but school & GPA aren’t everything! Your achievements competing in hackathons, launching startups, working in industry, volunteering for stretch projects, or building in your own time all add weight. So if you’ve shipped real work but don’t have a perfect résumé, apply anyway.

At Rokt, we choose to create a company that is as diverse and inclusive as the world we live in by attracting, growing and keeping the best talent. Equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

If this sounds like a role you’d enjoy, apply here, and you’ll hear from our recruiting team.

NOTE: Rokt only contacts candidates from @rokt.com addresses. We never request payment, bank details, or identity documents before a written offer, and we never interview solely over chat apps. Verify any role at rokt.com/careers if you’re unsure.

As one of the first engineers on PowerPlan’s Applied AI team, you’ll build the data foundation behind the AI solutions our own teams use every week, across finance, sales, professional services, and product. Most of the work is finding, cleaning, and defining the data each build needs, then picking the simplest structure that will hold it, and pairing with the team’s AI engineer to put larger solutions into the business’s hands.

PowerPlan builds the financial software behind the companies that keep the lights on, and nine in ten U.S. investor-owned utilities use our platform. The Applied AI team sits inside Strategic Initiatives, works closely with the executive leadership team, and brings that same standard of getting the numbers right to how the company itself runs. The standards you help set early will shape how every build after yours gets done.

Success will be measured by whether the AI solutions you build data for are in weekly use and run by the business, and by whether new builds start from trusted, shared data instead of fresh exports.

Learn how the company runs through its data in your first 30 days, deliver an owner-checked first catalog of critical data by the end of your first quarter, and keep it current enough by month 12 that business and technology leaders plan AI work from it.
Help set the team’s standards for data, connections, and code review from your first 30 days, including how AI tools connect to business systems read-only by default, no more complex than the job requires, and reviewed by IT and security.
Pair with the team’s AI engineer on a first build in your first quarter, lead the data on the first larger build into pilot by six months, and by month 12 deliver the data behind at least two larger AI solutions in weekly use and run by the business.
Agree on the first shared data sets in your first quarter, publish the first one by six months, and have at least two shared, governed data sets in use by more than one team or AI solution by month 12.
Within your first 12 months, retire hand-built recurring reports by defining the numbers once, so an AI tool can draft the commentary, answer questions, and flag what needs a person’s attention.
You have two to four years of professional experience as a data engineer, analytics engineer, or in a similar role where writing code to clean and model data was central to the job, or a master’s degree in a related field and at least one year of that experience.
You’ve turned messy, real data from a business system, a spreadsheet, or a set of documents into something people or an AI tool used, and you can walk us through what broke and how you fixed it.

You work in Git by habit, treat data access and documentation as part of the build, and write notes a business owner can follow.

jobs.title: Software Developer 2
jobs.description:
Software Developer 2

Location: Centennial, CO (In-Office)
Company: RefiJet
Reports to: Director of Software Development
The Opportunity

RefiJet processes a high volume of auto refinance applications every month across a network of 30+ lending partners. The software running that operation spans borrower-facing applications, lender integrations, and internal tools used by our operations teams. The quality, reliability, and usability of that software directly affects real financial outcomes for real people.
Software Developer 2 is the level where you stop needing the work handed to you fully defined. You already know how to ship. This role is about widening what you can be trusted with: features that touch more than one system, requirements that arrive incomplete, and problems where the right answer is not obvious from the ticket. You will work across frontend applications, backend services, APIs, lender integrations, and internal operations tools.
This level carries in both directions. You are still learning, and you still have people invested in your development: structured code review, a manager whose job includes your growth, and senior engineers who will make you better when you use them. You are also now someone other people learn from. You will mentor Software Developer 1 engineers, review their code with care rather than speed, and answer the questions that are still hard when you are new to a codebase. Carrying someone else is part of the job at this level, not an extra.
We are deliberately stack and platform agnostic. We care that you can think clearly, learn a codebase quickly, and write code other engineers can build on. We do not care which language or framework you learned first. The specific technologies you will work in are covered in the interview process, and they will change over the course of your career here. The fundamentals will not.
Location and schedule.
Plan on five days per week on site in Centennial, Colorado. We say that plainly instead of calling the role hybrid, because the mentoring and cross-team work this level depends on happens faster in person and because we would rather be clear now than surprise you at offer stage. One or two remote days per week may become available once you are established and performing well. You earn it, the Director of Software Development decides it, and no date is attached to it.
What You'll Do - Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Leadership

At this level, leadership means owning outcomes rather than tasks, and starting to make the engineers around you better.
Own the features and components assigned to you end to end, including design decisions within an agreed approach, testing, release, and support after release
Mentor Software Developer 1 engineers through pairing, code review, and onboarding, and treat their questions as part of your workload rather than an interruption
Review code as a contributor of useful feedback, not a rubber stamp. Catch the design problem, not only the style problem.
Push back on work that does not hold together, and propose the alternative rather than only naming the objection
Estimate your own work with enough accuracy that others can plan around it, and communicate a slipping estimate before the date, not after
Improve how the team works by strengthening documentation, tightening standards, and reducing recurring toil
Represent engineering credibly in conversations with product, operations, and other internal partners, including explaining technical constraints in terms a non-engineer can act on

Discovery & Execution

Deliver features across frontend applications, backend services, APIs, and internal tools, including work that spans more than one service or team boundary
Take a requirement that is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the questions that make it concrete, and turn it into a workable plan before writing code
Author specifications for your own work and review specifications written by others, under our spec-driven development practice in which a feature is specified in writing and agreed before it is built
Design and build API integrations, including work with external lending partner systems, with attention to error handling, retries, idempotency, and failure modes
Model and query data correctly, and understand the performance and integrity consequences of the schema and queries you write
Write and maintain automated tests that give the team real confidence, and recognize when a test is protecting behavior rather than only raising coverage
Debug production issues methodically, identify the actual cause, verify the fix, and record what you learned so the next person does not repeat it
Participate in release, deployment, monitoring, and production support for the systems you build
Use AI-assisted development tools as part of normal daily work, and remain fully accountable for every line you ship, whether you or a tool wrote it first

Growth & Optimization

What this level looks like when it is going well

First 90 days:
You are delivering defined features independently and your code review comments are useful to other people. You know the shape of our borrower, lender, and internal systems, and you can find your way into unfamiliar code without a guide.
First 6 months:
You take on a feature with unclear requirements and come back with a plan rather than a list of questions. You are the reviewer a Software Developer 1 wants on their pull request. You have improved something structural, not only shipped tickets.
First year:
You own a component or feature area that others rely on. You are trusted with work that touches lender integrations or borrower-facing flows. A Software Developer 1 is measurably better because of you, and you can name how.

What you will build skill in

System design at feature and service scope, including the tradeoffs between the obvious approach and the durable one
The business context behind our borrower, lender, and internal systems, deeply enough to spot when a requirement will not survive contact with reality
Performance, observability, and reliability work, including reading production signals rather than guessing
Secure development and correct handling of regulated borrower and lender data
Mentoring as a distinct skill, including how to give feedback that lands and how to let someone struggle productively
Technical writing, since specifications, design notes, and incident write-ups are how decisions survive past the conversation

Growth path

The ladder is Software Developer 1, Software Developer 2, Software Developer 3, Lead Software Developer. Each level has documented expectations. What separates them is the scope and independence of the work you can be trusted with, not years on your resume. You advance to Software Developer 3 when you can own ambiguous, cross-cutting problems, when your technical judgment is sought rather than checked, and when your effect on other engineers is visible. We promote from within, and we will tell you plainly where you stand against the next level.
Partnership & Compliance

Work directly with product stakeholders and operations partners to shape features that solve real business problems, not only to receive requirements from them
Coordinate with other engineers on work that crosses service or team boundaries, including agreeing on interfaces before both sides build
Support QA, testing, release, and post-release validation so features work as intended before they reach users
Follow and help enforce internal standards for source control, code quality, documentation, deployment, and team communication
Handle borrower and lender data responsibly and follow all internal security, privacy, and data handling requirements. We operate in a regulated industry. Careful data handling is a condition of the role, not a preference.
Never move production data into a non-production environment, share credentials, or work around a security control to save time. If a control is blocking legitimate work, escalate it and help fix the control.
Contribute to a collaborative engineering culture by being dependable, communicative, and open to feedback

Required Skills & Experience

This list is short and every item on it is real. If you meet these, apply.
Professional experience building and maintaining production web applications across both frontend and backend, with a track record of features you delivered end to end
Working proficiency in a modern backend language and a modern frontend framework, with enough depth to debug problems in both
Practical experience with REST APIs or service-to-service integration, including handling failures rather than only the happy path
Practical experience with relational databases, including writing queries you can reason about and schema changes you can defend
Experience writing automated tests and using them to ship with confidence
Experience debugging issues in a running production system
Comfortable working from written specifications, and able to identify when a specification is wrong or incomplete
Version control fluency with Git and collaborative development workflows
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain a technical tradeoff to someone who is not an engineer
Demonstrated ability to give and receive feedback constructively
Legally authorized to work in the United States, and able to work on site in Centennial, CO five days per week

Education:
No specific degree is required. A computer science or related degree, a bootcamp, self-directed learning, or equivalent practical experience are all acceptable paths. We evaluate demonstrated ability.
On experience level:
This role is scoped for roughly 2 to 5 years of professional experience. Range is a proxy, not the bar. If you are outside it in either direction and the rest of this description fits, apply anyway and let us make the call.
Nice to Have

None of the following is required, and their absence will not remove you from consideration.
Experience owning a feature area or service that other engineers depended on
Experience mentoring or onboarding a more junior engineer
Experience integrating with third-party or partner APIs where you did not control the other side
Experience with containerized or cloud-hosted environments and the deployment pipeline that reaches them
Experience with observability tooling, including tracing a real incident through logs and metrics
Experience using AI-assisted development tools with good judgment about when to trust them
Interest in fintech, lending platforms, or transaction-heavy software products
Experience with auto lending, auto refinancing, or consumer credit products.
Familiarity with loan origination systems (LOS), credit decisioning, or lending infrastructure.
Experience working with external partners or B2B clients in a product-led organization.

Compensation & Benefits

Base Salary:
$108,000 - $137,000 annually, commensurate with experience
Bonus:
Eligible for an annual performance-based bonus with a defined target percentage of base salary, tied to company and individual goals.
Benefits:
Comprehensive benefits including health, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k), PTO, career development opportunities, and the chance to join Denver's Best Place to Work (2024 & 2025) with a dynamic culture focused on internal promotion and employee growth.
Equal Opportunity Statement

Yield Solutions Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants.

Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

Design, train, validate, and launch models for behavior cloning and reinforcement learning
Build and maintain data ingestion, labeling, and management pipelines to ensure high-quality training datasets

Collaborate with simulation, systems, and infrastructure teams to integrate ML models into real-world autonomous systems
Deploy and debug these models in real-world environments, addressing practical issues such as latency, hardware constraints, and system integration

3+ years of practical experience applying Machine Learning with Deep Learning frameworks, such as PyTorch/Tensorflow/JAX to solve real-world problems
3+ years of professional experience building, deploying, and maintaining Machine Learning models in production environments

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

We are looking for a perception engineer to build features for our customers' analytics. This isn’t just a data science job. This is developing fundamental perception features to drive customer-facing platforms. What are the real-world challenges in measuring dig productivity from lidar/camera data? Can we modify existing perception systems to provide useful metrics for job sites? How do you measure safety over an entire site given perception systems? How do you re-identify the same objects across dozens of camera views on a site several city blocks wide, through dust and changing light?

What You’ll Do

Extend, modify and adapt existing perception signals for analytics needs
Work with customers to define and scope what is possible with advanced perception systems on-site
Deploy models and analytics directly to fleets of machines

MSc or advanced degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field
4+ years of professional experience shipping perception systems to production (ideally on robotic or other embedded platforms), with strong hands-on experience in a modeling framework (e.g. PyTorch)
Proficient in Python and comfortable reading and writing at least one systems language (e.g. C++, Rust)
Hands-on experience incorporating raw sensor data (camera, lidar, IMU) into learned pipelines
Solid grounding in 3D geometry, sensor calibration (intrinsics/extrinsics), coordinate transforms, and camera/image re-projection algorithms
Strong data analysis skills across statistical characterization of sensor data, corner-case and anomaly discovery, and evaluation design

Ways To Stand Out

One or more of the following:

Prior experience working with customers to understand perception data and analytics
Experience with the Rust programming language
Published work in top-tier venues such as ICRA, IROS, CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, CoRL, or RSS

Based in the Bay Area with the ability to be onsite at our SF office on a daily/weekly basis

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

The Mission

We’re looking for exceptional Software Engineers to build and scale our robotics simulation environment. Simulation is a critical foundation for autonomy at Bedrock - it allows us to validate end-to-end systems, evaluate complex and unsafe scenarios, and run testing at massive scale.

Our autonomy stack is deeply machine-learning–driven, and closing the sim-to-real gap is a core focus of this role. The simulator must accurately represent real-world physics - including terrain deformation for digging and earthmoving - while remaining efficient enough to support thousands of simulation runs. High-quality simulation directly accelerates robotics development, making this work central to our success.

What You’ll Do

Build and scale high-fidelity simulation environments for autonomous construction machines
Develop simulation systems that support ML-based autonomy, evaluation, and safety validation
Improve realism and performance to better reflect real-world behavior
Help guide our strategy in scene generation and neural rendering techniques
Write production-quality, hands-on code and build real simulation content—not just prototypes

Who You Are

Simulation spans many disciplines, and we don’t expect one person to do everything. Strong candidates typically bring:

A passion for large-scale, realistic simulation systems
Experience with advanced 3D simulation software
Experience evaluating systems and improving realism to support autonomy stacks
A hands-on mindset and enthusiasm for building core simulation algorithms and content

What We’re Looking For

Engineering, math, or physics degree, or computer science background with demonstrated interest and strength in math and physics
4+ years of professional experience in software engineering, with proven track record of building modular, maintainable, production-quality software systems in C++
2+ years of experience with one or more 3D engines or simulation frameworks, such as: Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Blender, Gazebo, Isaac Sim, Omniverse

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Rust or interest in learning it
Robotics simulation background
Experience with neural rendering techniques (Gaussian splats, NeRFs)

jobs.title: AI-First Software Developer - Softeon
jobs.description:
IFS is a billion-dollar revenue company with 6,000+ employees on all continents. Our leading AI technology is the backbone of our award-winning enterprise software solutions, enabling our customers to be their best when it really matters, at the Moment of Service™. Our commitment to internal AI adoption has allowed us to stay at the forefront of technological advancements, ensuring our colleagues can unlock their creativity and productivity, and our solutions are always cutting-edge.

IFS Softeon builds warehouse management and supply chain execution software (WMS, WES, distributed order management and the Elastic UI platform) for some of the most demanding fulfillment operations in the world.

At IFS, we are flexible, we are innovative, and we are focused not only on how we can engage with our customers but on how we can make a real change and have a worldwide impact. We celebrate diversity and are committed to an inclusive workforce that represents the many cultures, backgrounds and viewpoints of our customers, partners and communities.

We are looking for innovative and original thinkers to work in an environment where you can #MakeYourMoment, so that we can help others make theirs. Join Team Purple. Join IFS.

Job Description

Ship more of what customers need, faster, and prove every change works.

Our applications run the warehouses that get orders out the door on time. We are changing how that software gets built: AI agents and AI-assisted CI/CD help us deliver more functionality to our customers, faster, with higher quality.

We are looking for an AI-first developer: someone who treats AI agents as a team to direct, not a fancy autocomplete. You will pair deep Java engineering with hands-on experience building through agents to deliver great new functionality across our applications, and you will help set the standard for how the rest of engineering works this way. You know that speed only counts if it comes with proof, so automated testing, validation and agent-assisted review are part of how you ship every change.

What you will do

Deliver great product functionality. Design and build new features and enhancements across our Java applications (receiving, inventory, picking, replenishment, shipping, integrations and user experience) that customers value and rely on.
Build with agents every day. Use Claude Code and similar coding agents to plan, implement, refactor and test features. Break work into clear specs, give agents strong context, and know when to delegate and when to step in.
Author and maintain agent skills. Write and refine skills, prompts, tool definitions and MCP servers that encode Softeon's domain knowledge, such as Elastic UI form and flow authoring, WMS configuration and integration patterns.
Own a fully automated delivery pipeline. Build and run CI/CD where every change passes automated builds, unit and integration tests, static analysis, security scanning and AI agent code review before a human approves it.
Make quality provable. Build and extend automated validation (unit, API and Playwright end-to-end tests) so that AI-generated code, configuration and integrations are verified automatically, with evidence.
Operate what you ship. Build the telemetry, logging and monitoring your features need, and treat performance and reliability as product requirements rather than a late pass.
Modernize with confidence. Use agents to understand, refactor and modernize existing code, add missing test coverage, and pay down technical debt without slowing feature delivery.
Measure velocity and quality. Track cycle time, defect rates and escaped bugs, and use the data to keep improving how agents and pipelines are used.
Work with product and customers. Turn real warehouse and supply chain needs into well-specified, testable software, and talk with product managers, customers and Ops teams in their language.
Raise the bar for the team. Share patterns, review others' agent workflows, measure what works, and help colleagues become effective AI-first developers.

Why it is interesting

Agents can write code faster than any team can review it. The hard part is no longer typing; it is deciding what to build, giving agents the right context, and proving that what comes back is correct in a domain where a plausible answer can still stop a warehouse. That means designing the specs, skills, tests and pipeline gates that let a small team ship enterprise software at a pace that used to need a much larger one, and there is no settled playbook to copy.
You will do this on mature, mission-critical applications with real customers, real data and real operational stakes, which is a harder and more rewarding problem than a greenfield demo.

Frameworks and tools you will work with:

Languages & core

Java 17+, Spring / Spring Boot, REST and messaging APIs, SQL and relational databases

Front end

TypeScript, Angular, and Elastic UI, our metadata-driven UI platform (XSLT forms and flows rendered as JSON schema)

Scripting & extension

Groovy scripts and connectors, extension APIs and scaffolding for customer and partner modifications

AI & agents

Claude Code and other coding agents, agent skills, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, LLM APIs, evaluation of agent output

Quality

JUnit, API and integration testing, Playwright end-to-end tests, test data and fixtures, mutation testing

Delivery & DevSecOps

GitHub and GitHub Actions (or Jenkins / Azure DevOps), automated agent code review, static analysis, security scanning, SBOM, Docker, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code

Operations

Logging, telemetry, monitoring and observability tooling across cloud environments

Qualifications

Required

2+ years of hands-on AI and agent-based development: building production software with coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot agents or similar, and/or building LLM-powered features and agents (tool use, retrieval, MCP, evaluation).
Expert-level Java: modern Java (17+), Spring/Spring Boot, REST APIs, multithreading, performance tuning and clean, maintainable design.
5+ years of professional software development, with a track record of building, shipping and operating production systems.
Strong experience in supply chain, automation, MRP or ERP systems. You understand how orders, inventory, materials and fulfillment flow through enterprise systems, and you can spot an answer that looks plausible but is operationally wrong.
CI/CD and DevOps fluency: Git-based workflows, pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Azure DevOps or similar), containers (Docker, Kubernetes) and infrastructure as code.
Automated testing, observability and continuous delivery as part of how you build, not a separate phase.
Prompt and context engineering skills: clear written specs, structured prompts and the judgment to evaluate and correct agent output.
Comfortable across the boundary: you can write the front-end, service and database code a feature needs end to end.
Solid fundamentals in relational databases and SQL, system design, and secure coding practices.
Permanent resident of the United States, legally authorized to work in the US without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

Also valuable

A platform where behavior is configured through data or metadata rather than written in code, such as low-code, rules engines or schema-driven UI.
Modern TypeScript and Angular (or React), including component architecture and design-system work.
Direct experience with warehouse management (WMS), warehouse execution (WES), transportation management (TMS) or MRP/ERP platforms, as a developer, implementer or operator.
Experience with warehouse automation: conveyors, sortation, pick-to-light, AMRs, goods-to-person systems or their control software.
Mobile or progressive web applications, including RF/handheld devices, offline behavior and poor connectivity.
Experience building MCP servers, custom agent tooling or AI-powered developer workflows.
Familiarity with XSLT and Groovy, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure or GCP).
Based in the US Eastern or Central time zone.

How we work

AI-first by default. Agents are part of the team; you are responsible for their output.
No change ships without proof. Automated tests, agent review and validation evidence on every pull request.
Close to customers. We learn from warehouse floors and Ops leaders, not just tickets.
Small, senior and fast. High ownership, low ceremony, measurable results.

What success looks like

First 30 days: you ship production changes through the full agent-assisted pipeline and know our Java platform and WMS domain.
First 90 days: you own a feature area end to end, have contributed new agent skills or pipeline checks, and have measurably sped up delivery without lowering quality.
First year: you have delivered significant product functionality and are a go-to person for AI-first engineering practices across Softeon engineering.

Location and eligibility

This is a remote, US-based role. Candidates must be permanent residents of the United States. We prefer candidates in the Eastern or Central time zones to support collaboration with our teams and customers. Occasional travel to customer sites or company offices may be required.

Additional Information

Flexible paid time off, including sick and holiday
Medical, dental, & vision insurance
401K with Company contribution

jobs.title: Application Engineer
jobs.description:
Membrion is a growing clean technology company transforming how industries manage wastewater. Our proprietary electro-ceramic desalination (ECD) technology helps industrial customers treat challenging wastewater streams, recover valuable resources, and reduce the environmental and financial costs of water treatment. Working across industries including semiconductor manufacturing, food and beverage, and consumer packaged goods, we're bringing innovative treatment solutions into real-world industrial operations.

Are you an engineer who loves solving problems that don't have obvious answers?

We're looking for an Applications Engineer who can turn complex customer challenges into practical, technically sound treatment solutions.
Working closely with our Sales, Technology, Engineering, Product, and Customer Success teams, you'll evaluate customer wastewater processes, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop integrated treatment solutions that balance technical performance, cost, and operational realities.

Our projects typically range from $500,000 to $5 million, and no two applications are quite the same. You'll need to think creatively, understand how different processes and equipment work together, and develop solutions that can be successfully integrated into existing industrial facilities.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the details, challenging assumptions, and taking ownership of problems through to resolution. You'll have the independence to manage your work, the support of an experienced technical team, and the opportunity to see your solutions put into practice.

What You Will Do

Understand the Customer Application

• Gather and evaluate wastewater analyses, operating data, treatment objectives, site constraints, and existing infrastructure through customer discussions, records, and site inputs.
• Identify data gaps, likely root causes, ECD applicability, and technical risks; define the additional information or testing needed to advance the opportunity.
• Establish a traceable design basis that clearly distinguishes verified data, assumptions, and uncertainties.

Develop Integrated Treatment Solutions

Develop creative, practical treatment concepts that integrate ECD with appropriate pretreatment and downstream processes, considering existing customer equipment, infrastructure, and operational constraints.
Prepare process flow diagrams, mass balances, preliminary P&IDs where appropriate, and equipment and membrane sizing.
Evaluate treatment alternatives based on performance, recovery, utility requirements, capital and operating costs, and sensitivity to changing feed conditions.
Translate bench-scale and pilot results into practical design inputs, collaborating with Technology and Engineering to address system integration, safety, constructability, and operability before customer commitments.

Prepare Credible Technical Proposals

Prepare technical scopes, system descriptions, process drawings, equipment information, and supported performance expectations, with clear assumptions and exclusions.
Create customer proposals that balance customer technical requirements with project execution planning and risk mitigation.
Support Sales in customer technical discussions by explaining design choices, treatment tradeoffs, and the value of the proposed solution.
Check consistency across calculations, drawings, costs, scope, and performance claims; incorporate review feedback and maintain clear decision and revision records.

Deliver Reliably and Improve Future Applications

Manage assigned milestones across multiple opportunities, communicate progress proactively, and escalate missing inputs or technical blockers early.
Provide Engineering and Customer Success with clear and complete handoff documentation covering the design basis, scope boundaries, decisions, and unresolved items.
Use and improve approved calculators, templates, and workflows. Capture validated application learnings and share recurring customer needs with Product and the broader team.

Qualifications:

We're interested in Applications Engineers who bring strong technical judgment, curiosity, and a practical approach to solving problems. While experience in industrial wastewater treatment is particularly valuable, we recognize that relevant skills can be developed through different engineering backgrounds and career paths.
Experience in applications engineering, process engineering, or a related technical role, ideally involving industrial water or wastewater treatment.
Strong analytical and creative problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technical challenges and develop practical solutions.
An understanding of industrial processes, equipment integration, and the operational requirements of treatment systems.
Knowledge of water chemistry, mass balances, treatment performance, fouling, scaling, and operating cost considerations.
Ability to develop and review engineering calculations, process flow diagrams, technical specifications, and proposal documentation.
Sound engineering judgment, including the ability to recognize incomplete information, challenge assumptions, and identify when further technical validation is required.
Strong written communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with technical and commercial colleagues.
A proactive, self-directed approach to work, with the ability to manage competing priorities and take ownership of deliverables.
Comfort working in a collaborative, predominantly remote environment where communication, initiative, and follow-through are essential.

Experience That Would Be Particularly Valuable

Direct experience with industrial wastewater treatment systems, particularly membrane processes such as UF, NF, RO, or related technologies.
Experience designing, sizing, or specifying packaged process equipment, including skid-mounted or containerized systems.
Hands-on experience with equipment commissioning, field startup, operational troubleshooting, or supporting equipment integration at customer facilities.
Experience preparing technical proposals, process flow diagrams, preliminary P&IDs, or CAPEX/OPEX evaluations.
Experience with industrial applications in semiconductor manufacturing, food and beverage, or consumer packaged goods.
A background in chemical, environmental, mechanical, or related engineering disciplines.

We value practical experience and demonstrated capability over any particular educational pathway. Candidates with transferable experience and a willingness to learn are encouraged to apply.
You'll Thrive in This Role If You...

Love solving complex technical problems, especially when the answer isn't immediately obvious.
Take initiative, work independently, and follow problems through to resolution.
Can balance technical detail with practical commercial and operational considerations.
Enjoy collaborating with people from different technical and commercial backgrounds.
Want to see your engineering work translate into real-world environmental and operational impact.

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in recognizing the experience, expertise, and contributions of our team. We offer a competitive compensation package and the opportunity to be part of a growing company working on meaningful environmental challenges.
Base Salary:
$90,000–145,000 USD annually, depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.
Work Arrangement:
Predominantly remote, with opportunities to collaborate in person with colleagues and customers.
Travel:
Approximately 25–30%, including customer site visits and occasional travel to our Seattle facility.
Health & Wellness:
Medical, dental and vision coverage through CAMPS Health Trust, starting the first of the month after you join, with no long waiting period. Also includes life and AD&D insurance, optional additional life coverage, and an Employee Assistance Program.

Why Membrion?

Solve problems that matter.
Industrial wastewater treatment is a complex challenge, and the solutions aren't always obvious. At Membrion, we're developing technology that helps industries treat difficult wastewater streams, recover valuable resources, and reduce their environmental impact. Your engineering work will have a tangible, real-world purpose.
Work with genuinely innovative technology.
Our electro-ceramic desalination (ECD) technology is opening up new possibilities for industrial wastewater treatment. You'll work on challenging applications where conventional approaches don't always deliver, combining established engineering principles with creative thinking to develop better solutions.
See your ideas become reality.
This isn't a role where your work ends with a calculation or a drawing. You'll help develop solutions that become real equipment, integrated into operating industrial facilities. You'll have opportunities to see your work in action and understand the impact of your engineering decisions.
Have the freedom to figure things out.
We're a growing company, and we value people who take initiative, ask good questions, and find ways forward. You'll have the autonomy to own your work, the support of experienced colleagues, and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution without layers of bureaucracy.
Work with people who care about getting it right.
We're a collaborative team of engineers, scientists, and commercial professionals who bring different perspectives to the same challenges. We value curiosity, accountability, practical problem-solving, and people who are willing to roll up their sleeves and help each other succeed.

Our Core Values

See What Isn't Obvious

Relentlessly Flow Like a River

Obnoxiously Reliable

All in This Together

Better Each Day

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About The Role

We are building highly complex interfaces for the bleeding edge of robotics and autonomy. A customer's first real contact with Bedrock technology is the interface that mediates the autonomous machine and their intentions. It is critical that the software they interact with is as magical as the autonomy that powers the machine.

In this foundational role, you will establish our core UI interactions and workflows. You will deeply own our software stack, pushing the boundaries of what is possible across a variety of browser and native environments to deliver ultra-low latency control over heavy machinery.

Also, you get to drive 100,000 lb excavators.

Partner closely with robotics, autonomy, and backend engineers to translate high-dimensional machine data into intuitive operational workflows.

Required Qualifications

6+ years of professional experience driving the design, architecture, and implementation of highly complex, business-critical frontend applications.
Deep expertise in shipping iOS and Android apps.
A strong understanding of network management, memory management, and rendering performance.
Experience building sophisticated applications that handle massive datasets, complex state, real-time data streaming (WebSockets, WebRTC), and asynchronous flows.
Strong product and systems thinking: the ability to design architectures from first principles and craft polished, "magical" user experiences for power users.
Comfort deeply owning a software stack and navigating the ambiguity of rapid prototyping in a fast-paced startup environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience pushing performance boundaries in native and cross-platform (Swift, Kotlin, KMP, React Native, etc).
Background in 3D visualization, rendering, or scene-based interfaces using WebGL/WebGPU, Three.js, CesiumJS or similar technologies.
Experience working with geospatial tooling, massive map datasets, or GIS systems (e.g., handling GeoTIFFs, WGS84, custom projections).
Familiarity with ultra-low latency workflows, real-time video streaming pipelines, or interfaces operating in constrained edge-network environments.

jobs.title: Sr. Backend Software Engineer (Infrastructure ML Ops)
jobs.description:
At Philo, we’re a group of technology and product people who set out to build the future of television, marrying the best in modern technology with the most compelling medium ever invented — in short, we’re building the TV experience that we’ve always wanted for ourselves. In practice this means leveraging cloud delivery, modern tech stacks, machine learning, and hand-crafted native app experiences on all of our platforms. We aim to deliver a rock solid experience on the streaming basics, while cooking up next generation multi-screen and multi-user playback experiences.

Senior Backend Software Engineer (Infrastructure MLOps)

The infrastructure team at Philo builds the foundation for a 24/7 live and on-demand streaming product serving video to our growing subscriber base. It provides a platform that enables groups across the company – such as video delivery, product, support, and analytics – to do their best work easily and smoothly. Our systems are highly distributed, horizontally scalable and run in the cloud on Kubernetes. We continuously test and deploy our code and closely monitor the health and performance of our production environment.

We are seeking an enthusiastic Infrastructure MLOps Software Engineer to help us build and improve the ML infrastructure at Philo. We are building out ML and LLM infrastructure and this role will be pivotal in setting direction, adopting best practices, and shipping infrastructure that will be used across the company.

As a sample, the ML infrastructure supports teams like Discovery in building content recommendation models that will help our users find more favorite shows from the large Philo catalog. The engineering team is designing and developing our own agent harnesses to support coding and empowering everyone at the company to get answers across our code bases, analytics, logs, and communication tools. The video player team is using LLMs to classify ads and label our video catalog so that users have a better experience. You’ll build the serving, evaluation and platform infrastructure that these workloads depend on.

Responsibilities

Manage the core infrastructure at Philo with a focus on supporting ML and LLM workloads. This infrastructure is relied on by a large subscriber base of Philo’s product as well as internal stakeholders across the company.
Design, build, and maintain cloud infrastructure components (AWS and Kubernetes) using a combination of in-house technology and open source software.
Build and scale model serving and inference infrastructure for both real-time recommendation models and LLM workloads — including model servers (e.g. NVIDIA Triton), LLM inference engines (e.g. vLLM, TGI, TensorRT-LLM), autoscaling, and latency/throughput optimization.
Manage GPU and accelerator infrastructure on Kubernetes — scheduling, capacity and quota management, and cost optimization across on-demand and spot capacity.
Design, build, and maintain monitoring and observability systems — spanning both system health and model quality (drift, evaluation, and online performance) — that enable Philo engineers and the support team to gain insight and to discover and debug issues.
Build and operate model evaluation infrastructure: offline and online eval pipelines, golden/regression datasets, LLM-as-judge harnesses, A/B testing and experimentation, and feedback/ground-truth loops
Design, build, and maintain CI/CD systems enabling Philo engineers to create pipelines to test and deploy their code.
Establish tools, methods and best practices for other Philo engineers interfacing with the Philo ML infrastructure. Ensure reliability, security, and scalability of the Philo platform. Promote Infrastructure as Code.
Work closely with other Philo engineers to deploy and instrument software systems.
Drive evaluation, selection, and integration of third-party vendor systems and work closely with vendors to configure and manage them.

Qualifications

8+ years of software development and infrastructure management experience.
4+ years of experience developing and deploying ML systems at scale across training and inference
Experience working with distributed systems and an understanding of microservices architecture principles.
Experience with Linux and containerized (i.e. Docker) environments.
Experience managing cloud computing environments (AWS or GCP) and configuring cloud services e.g. CloudWatch, Route 53, RDS, ElastiCache, SQS, ALB/NLB/ELB, VPC networking, IAM security.
Experience with container orchestration platforms (i.e. Kubernetes), and familiarity with running GPU/accelerated workloads on them (e.g. NVIDIA device plugin, MIG, timeslicing).
Strong understanding of networking and internet application protocols including, but not limited to TCP/IP, DNS, and HTTP.
Strong understanding of network and application security principles and best practices.
Familiarity or hands-on experience with configuration management systems and Infrastructure as Code (e.g. Terraform, CloudFormation).
Familiarity or hands-on experience with Monitoring/Observability systems (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, TICK/InfluxDB, Fluentd, ELK, Datadog).
Familiarity or hands-on experience with CI/CD automation systems e.g. Jenkins, Gitlab.
Experience with relational and non-relational databases and familiarity with modern data warehousing and querying.
Proficient in writing, testing, and profiling software in Golang, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++, Ruby, Python or similar programming languages.
Experience and aptitude for collaborating and communicating with internal and external stakeholders in both business and technical roles.

A strong candidate may also have one or more of these:

Hands-on experience optimizing inference — dynamic/continuous batching, quantization, KV-cache management, or GPU memory tuning — for low-latency or highthroughput serving.
Experience with ML platform tooling: model registry and experiment tracking (e.g. MLflow, Weights & Biases), feature stores (e.g. Feast, Tecton), and pipeline/workflow orchestration (e.g. Airflow, Dagster, Kubeflow, Ray, Metaflow).
Experience building model evaluation, monitoring, or experimentation systems — including drift detection, LLM-as-judge, or A/B testing for models.
Experience with LLMOps: inference gateways/routers (e.g. LiteLLM), hosted model APIs (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic), RAG pipelines, vector databases (e.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate), and prompt/version management.
Experience building or operating agent harnesses or tool-using LLM applications in production.
Experience with data and model versioning (e.g. DVC, LakeFS) and data/labeling pipelines.
Experience with cost management / FinOps for GPU and inference workloads

We are language agnostic, but most of our backend code is written in Golang, Ruby and TypeScript, with some C++ and Python. Our services run on Kubernetes, and we practice continuous deployment across all of our systems.

More About Philo

At Philo, we’re a company that puts people first—both our subscribers and our team. We empower our colleagues to do their best work while supporting one another in pursuing shared goals. We value pragmatism, pride in our work, and passion, with transparency and openness as fundamental parts of our culture.

We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility as we grow the Philo team and shape the future of TV. We believe that a diverse range of voices and perspectives enables us to innovate faster and create the best experiences for our subscribers. Philo is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to supporting every candidate and employee. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the process, please email recruiting@philo.com
and we’ll work with you to meet your needs.

Philo offers 70+ top-rated networks, including AMC, BET, CMT, Comedy Central, Discovery Channel, Food Network, Hallmark Channel, HGTV, HISTORY, Investigation Discovery, Lifetime, MTV, Nickelodeon, OWN, VH1, We TV, and more. It also includes all the groundbreaking originals and blockbuster movies available with AMC+ and access to HBO Max Basic With Ads and discovery+. Our service also includes 100+ free channels and premium add-ons like STARZ and MGM+.

Our extensive library boasts over 85,000 titles, and our unlimited DVR allows users to save their favorite shows and movies for up to a year, skipping ads for a seamless viewing experience. Stream on up to three devices simultaneously, whether on your phone, tablet, laptop, or TV using Roku, Apple TV, Fire TV, Samsung TV, Android TV, Vizio TV, or Chromecast.

Philo is headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Cambridge, MA. Our leadership team includes alums from HBO, Tubi, and Meraki, and is backed by NEA and industry partners like Warner Brothers Discovery, Paramount, AMC, and A&E.

Join us at Philo and be part of a team that's shaping the future of TV!

About The Opportunity

Major duties and responsibilities

ECMA cARMY onboarding

Run the ECMA intake end to end:
tenant request package and account vending
Control Tower / Landing Zone Accelerator guardrails within the ECMA baseline
IAM Identity Center federation to the Army identity provider
VPN and boundary connectivity requests
Prepare and track the Government artifacts the program depends on: the Authorizing Official designation memo, the ISSO appointment and the inherited-control matrix.

Maintain a dependency tracker for every Government-paced item, with owner, submission date and escalation path, reported weekly.
SIPR option: repeat onboarding for IL6, covering the second Authorizing Official chain, SIPR identity binding, the DISA SIPRNet circuit request and classified break-glass access.

Landing zone and environments

Deliver reusable, parameterized landing-zone infrastructure code for cARMY: account baseline, service control policies, centralized CloudTrail/Config/log archive, Security Hub, GuardDuty, network baseline with VPC endpoints, and the KMS key hierarchy. NIPR and SIPR must differ only by parameters.
Stand up NIPR development, test and staging by about month 4, and multi-region production by about month 7. Production includes Global Tables and Route 53 failover, with recovery time and recovery point objectives documented and demonstrated.
Integrate with the program's AWS SAM application layer through a defined contract: exported VPC, subnet, endpoint, KMS and logging identifiers. The engagement does not fork or replace the application templates.

IL5 boundary, STIG and ATO acceleration

Define the IL5 authorization boundary: boundary and data-flow diagrams, ports, protocols and services, and the split of inherited, shared and system-specific controls with cARMY.
Deliver NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 conformance packs and DISA STIG automation for Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and the landing-zone services, with evidence the RMF team can load into eMASS.
Provide System Security Plan templates pre-filled for cARMY-inherited controls, and support the SSP amendment, eMASS submission and SCA-V coordination.
Set up DoD PKI certificate distribution and rotation.

Continuous ATO

Provide the continuous-ATO playbook and help stand up the OSCAL/ConMon pipeline: Config and Security Hub feeds, drift detection, the ConMon dashboard and the 30-day evidence period.
Support the Authorizing Official signature campaign toward NIPR continuous ATO at month 12.

Migration into cARMY

Plan and execute the move of the demonstrator from the commercial GovCloud account into cARMY: AWS DMS or DynamoDB export and import, cut-over and rollback runbooks, and a full rehearsal. Workloads land in development, test and staging first, then production.

Knowledge transfer and exit

Deliver runbooks and architecture decision records for every landing-zone design decision.

Qualifications

ECMA cARMY onboarding experience: has taken at least one prior Army tenant through ECMA cARMY onboarding to first authenticated deployment. This is the qualification that defines the role.
GovCloud landing zones at IL5: Control Tower and/or Landing Zone Accelerator, AWS Organizations and service control policies, IAM Identity Center, centralized logging, Security Hub, GuardDuty, AWS Config conformance packs.
DoD authorization: DoD Cloud Computing SRG, RMF, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and eMASS, with direct experience of Authorizing Official and SCA-V review cycles. Prior continuous-ATO or ConMon delivery is strongly preferred.
Infrastructure as code: production-quality CloudFormation / AWS SAM. CDK (Landing Zone Accelerator) or Terraform is acceptable where the output integrates with the SAM application layer.
Serverless platform depth: Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB (Global Tables, point-in-time recovery, Streams, capacity), EventBridge, SQS, KMS, WAF, VPC endpoints, Route 53 failover.
Data migration: AWS DMS and DynamoDB export and import.
Hardening: DISA STIG automation for cloud and serverless resources.
Experience and education: 10+ years in cloud infrastructure, including 5+ years in AWS GovCloud or DoD environments. Bachelor's in IT, CS or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Certifications

AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate or higher is required. This is the labor-category minimum and cannot be waived.
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional is expected for this engagement.
